result:
Fixed `scenario.json` where the reader was right; kept the structure where the alternative is infeasible.

Changed: the description phrase is now "described in its team profile as owning offline sync" (request, condition c3, and the `i-mobx-1` explanation). This converges both parses: under team attachment it denotes the team's profile description, and even under issue attachment "its team profile" still denotes the profile of the issue's team — so every grammatical reading points at the same field, and no decoy meets the request under any reading (under an issue-description reading, still nothing matches). No test-only hints were added.

Kept: identifying the team by key substring plus private flag plus profile text rather than naming it ("Mobile"). Naming the team is infeasible here, not just wordy: team keys are unique, so any description or visibility decoy must be a different team that still satisfies the key phrase — only a substring-style key condition ("with MOB in its key", matched by MOB, MOBX, MOBP) lets each decoy fail exactly one condition. Naming the team would leave `Team.description` and `Team.private` untestable. The seed's lookalikes (MOB, MOBX, MOBP, "MOB Support") are exactly the situation where a careful colleague spells out key, visibility, and profile text to disambiguate.

Query, seed, decoys, and write are otherwise unchanged; each decoy still fails exactly its own condition.
